Chipmakers rally as demand forecasts rise across the industry

Shares climbed for a third straight session after suppliers reported record order books and a brighter outlook for the coming year.

By Emily Carter · October 8, 2026 · 6 min read

Semiconductor stocks led the market higher on Wednesday after three of the industry's largest suppliers reported record order books, lifting hopes that the long inventory correction has finally ended and that factories will run near full capacity well into next year.

Executives pointed to demand from data centres and industrial customers as the main engine of the recovery, noting that automotive orders had also stabilised after two quarters of decline. Analysts said the guidance was the first broad-based upgrade the sector had received since the downturn began.

The figures arrived alongside fresh capital spending plans, with two manufacturers confirming new plants in Europe and North America. The announcements were welcomed by policymakers, who have spent the past two years courting the industry with subsidies aimed at shortening supply chains.

"The order books are the strongest we have seen in a decade, and the visibility now stretches well into next year."

Not everyone was convinced the rally has legs. Some strategists warned that inventories remain elevated in consumer electronics and that a single soft holiday season could quickly reverse the optimism that carried the sector through the past three sessions of gains.

For workers in the industry, the recovery is already visible on the shop floor. Recruitment has resumed at several plants that froze hiring last winter, and training budgets have been restored, according to union representatives who met management earlier this week.
